section.title: Chapter review and discovery problems
section.p: Chapter 1 began with motion. It asked how to pass between velocity and distance, slope and area, difference and sum.

Chapter 2 built the language that this question needs. We used the real line to measure nearness, functions to record dependence, graphs to see geometric behavior, and models to connect formulas with real applications. We also learned that a graph on a screen is only evidence, not proof.
The next chapter returns to the original motion problem. But now we are ready to say what near means.

row.cell: limits need a precise language of closeness
unbroken pieces of the real line
distance from 0, or distance between two numbers
error is measured by inequalities such as |A-T|\lt \varepsilon
the real line has no gaps
one allowed output for each allowed input
calculus studies how outputs change when inputs change
derivative and limit questions must respect where a function is defined
a picture of all input-output pairs
slope, sign, roots, and behavior become visible
the chain rule will come from this structure
logarithms, inverse trig functions, and inverse rates depend on this idea
a function chosen to represent a situation
calculus measures change and accumulation in models

subsection.title: Concept check: function versus formula
subsection.p: Answer these without a calculator unless a problem explicitly asks for one. Use complete sentences when the question asks for an explanation.

li.p: Explain the difference between the intervals (2,5), [2,5], and [2,5). Which endpoints are included in each?
Why do we never write [2,\infty] as an interval?
Explain why |x-a|\lt \varepsilon means that x is within distance \varepsilon of a.
Write |x-7|\lt 0.01 as a double inequality.
Explain why the formula f(x)=x^2 does not completely describe a function until the domain is known.
Give two different functions that use the same formula x^2 but have different ranges.
A table gives the temperature of a cup of tea at times 0,1,2,3,4. Does the table automatically define the temperature at t=2.5? Explain.
The equation x^2+y^2=1 does not define y as a function of x on [-1,1]. Explain why.
The upper semicircle y=\sqrt{1-x^2} does define y as a function of x. What is its domain? What is its range?
Explain why h(x)=\frac{x^2-1}{x-1} is not the same function as p(x)=x+1 when p has domain \mathbb{R}.
What does the vertical line test check?
What does the horizontal line test check?
Explain why f^{-1}(x) usually does not mean \frac{1}{f(x)}.
Suppose f(3)=10. What point is on the graph of f? If f has an inverse, what corresponding point is on the graph of f^{-1}?
Why does order matter in a composition such as f(g(x))?
Why are radians the natural angle measure for calculus?
A graphing utility shows that a function appears positive in the window [-10,10]. Does that prove the function is positive for all real x? Explain.
What is a residual in a modeling problem?
A model fits five measured data points exactly. Why might it still be a poor model?
The rational numbers contain fractions between any two fractions. Why does that fact alone not make the rational number line complete?

subsection.title: Catalog practice: recognizing function families
subsection.p: Classify each model as linear, power-law, polynomial, rational, algebraic, trigonometric, exponential, or logarithmic. Then state a natural domain suggested by the context.

li.p: The cost of renting a bike is 12 dollars plus 4 dollars per hour: C(t)=12+4t.
The area of a circle of radius r is A(r)=\pi r^2.
A population doubles every 6 hours: P(t)=P_0\,2^{t/6}.
The height of a Ferris wheel rider is H(t)=18+15\sin\left(\frac{\pi t}{20}\right).
The average cost per item is A(x)=5+\frac{200}{x}.
The upper half of a circle of radius 5 is y=\sqrt{25-x^2}.
The time needed for an amount A to double under compound growth is described using \ln 2.
A projectile height model is h(t)=-16t^2+80t+5.
Prove that for \varepsilon\gt 0, |x-a|\lt \varepsilon \iff a-\varepsilon\lt x\lt a+\varepsilon.
Give an example of a curve that fails the vertical line test.
Give an example of a function that fails the horizontal line test.
Give an example of a formula that simplifies algebraically but still has a missing input in its original form.
Give an example of a piecewise rule that does not define a function because one input receives two outputs.

subsection.title: Technology questions
subsection.p: These problems are about using technology carefully. Use a graphing calculator or computer graphing tool when needed.

li.p: Graph f(x)=x^3-6x in the window [-1,1]\times[-6,6], and then in [-3,3]\times[-10,10]. What does the wider window reveal?
Graph h(x)=\frac{x^2-1}{x-1} and \ell(x)=x+1 in the same window. What difference might the screen hide?
Graph f(x)=\sin(100\pi x) on [0,1]. Try different sample settings. Explain why a poor sample can make this function look like 0.
Use a calculator to evaluate Q(h)=\frac{\sqrt{1+h}-1}{h} for h=10^{-2}, 10^{-4}, 10^{-8}, 10^{-12}. Compare with \frac{1}{\sqrt{1+h}+1}. What does this show about roundoff?
Find a graphing window in which g(x)=x^2+0.001\sin(1000x) looks almost like f(x)=x^2. Then zoom in until the oscillation becomes visible.
A graph suggests that x^2-2x+2\gt 0 for all real x. Prove the claim algebraically by completing the square.

subsection.title: Project: fit a simple model to data
subsection.p: A cup of coffee is placed in a room whose temperature is 22^\circ\text{C}. The table shows measured coffee temperatures.

figure.caption: The coffee cools toward room temperature. A good model should respect that long-term behavior.

li.p: Explain why a linear model may be reasonable for a short time but unreasonable forever.
Let E(t)=T(t)-22 be the excess temperature above the room. Complete the excess temperature values at each measurement time.
Compute the consecutive ratios \frac{E(t+5)}{E(t)}. Are they roughly constant?
Use the first two data points to build a model of the form T(t)=22+A\,b^{t/5}. Find A and b.
Use your model to predict the coffee temperature after 30 minutes.
Compute the residuals \text{measured temperature} - \text{predicted temperature} at the measured times.
Does the model overpredict, underpredict, or stay fairly balanced?
Explain why the horizontal line T=22 should be a long-term guide for the model.
Optional. Compare your exponential cooling model with a linear model made from the first and last data points. Which model gives a more reasonable prediction after 2 hours?
Same formula, different story. Consider y=x^2 on domains \mathbb{R}, [0,\infty), [-2,2], and [1,3]. For each domain, find the range and decide whether the function has an inverse.
A hidden composition. Write each function as a composition of simpler functions: \sqrt{3x+1}, (5-x^2)^4, \ln(1+x^2), and \sin(2x-7). Name the inside and outside functions.
How close is close? For Q(h)=4+h, find a condition on h that guarantees |Q(h)-4|\lt 0.001. Then do the same for R(h)=12+6h+h^2 under the extra assumption |h|\lt 1.
A graph that fools the eye. Find two functions that look nearly identical in a wide graphing window but have different behavior when you zoom in. Explain the difference.

Model choice. Create a table of six data points that would suggest a linear model. Then create a different table of six data points that would suggest an exponential model. Explain how differences or ratios reveal the pattern.
Rational approximations to \sqrt{2}. Use decimal intervals of length 0.1, 0.01, 0.001, 0.0001 that contain \sqrt{2}. Write the nested intervals. What real number do they trap?
Punctured intervals. Explain why the difference quotient \frac{f(a+h)-f(a)}{h} is naturally studied on a punctured interval around h=0, rather than on an interval that includes h=0.

The first limit proof hiding in Chapter 1. For s(t)=t^2, the average velocity from t=2 to t=2+h is 4+h. Given an allowed error \varepsilon\gt 0, find a condition on h that guarantees |(4+h)-4|\lt \varepsilon. Write your answer in the form 0\lt |h|\lt \delta.

subsection.title: Hook: limits make near into mathematics
subsection.p: The last problem is the doorway to the next chapter.
For s(t)=t^2, the average velocity from t=2 to t=2+h is 4+h (h\neq 0).
As h gets close to 0, the average velocity gets close to 4. Chapter 2 gave us the language to make that sentence sharper:
So if we want the output error to be less than \varepsilon, we can demand 0\lt |h|\lt \varepsilon.
This is the shape of a limit. The input is allowed to approach a forbidden or special value. The output is forced into any desired error bound.
The next chapter gives this idea its name.
